name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Build a self-review loop where every prompt update triggers an automated review of the same task batch that triggered the update. This keeps quality high by catching regressions immediately, not after 500 new tasks pile up. Trade-off: we accept slower updates for individual prompts because the review step adds latency, but the trade is worth it to prevent bad changes from spreading.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just slower updates—it’s that testing 500 tasks after every prompt tweak guarantees we’ll drown in false positives. A better alternative: batch prompt updates by semantic similarity, then test only the affected task clusters. Settle it by running a controlled A/B where we compare regression rates between immediate vs. batched reviews over 100 updates.

name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Run the new prompt against a fresh, diverse batch of 500 tasks *before* deploying it. This catches regressions early and proves the change actually improves quality, not just tweaks wording. Trade-off: we delay the prompt update by hours while the batch runs, but that’s cheaper than fixing a broken prompt after 5000 tasks fail.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just delayed deployment—it’s that testing 500 tasks *after* every prompt tweak turns regression hunting into a full-time job, drowning us in noise when a single bad batch could skew results. A better alternative: test only the *semantically closest* task clusters to the prompt change, then expand only if the delta shows real impact. Settle it by running a controlled A/B where we compare the narrow-test approach against Sprocket’s full-batch method, measuring both false-positive rates and actual quality gains.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Run a controlled A/B test where prompt updates are batched by semantic similarity and tested only on the affected task clusters, comparing against the current prompt on a fresh 500-task sample.

Result must deliver: clear evidence of quality impact (regression or improvement) with false-positive risk minimized.
